p.src: Wu Song then brought Kong Liang to appeal to Lu Zhishen and Yang Zhi, begging them to rescue his elder brother Kong Ming and his uncle Kong Bin. Lu Zhishen at once proposed mustering the forces of the three mountains and marching out to attack. Yang Zhi said, “If we mean to attack Qingzhou, only a great host of troops will be enough to take it. I know the great name of Song Gongming of Liangshan Marsh. Throughout the rivers and lakes they call him Song Jiang, the Timely Rain; moreover, Huyan Zhuo is an enemy of theirs. Let our brothers’ men and those of the Kong brothers join together, while I wait here until the forces of Peach Blossom Mountain are fully assembled; meanwhile, we shall go and attack Qingzhou. Brother Kong Liang, you must ride through the night in person to Liangshan Marsh and invite Song Gongming down. Then we can combine our strength to attack the city. That is the best plan. Besides, Third Brother Song is very close to you. What do you brothers think?” Lu Zhishen said, “That is exactly what we should do. One day I hear someone praising Third Brother Song, and the next day someone else does the same. It is a pity that I have never met him. People have talked of him until my ears are nearly deaf. He must be a true man indeed to have won such fame throughout the realm. Once before, when Commandant Hua and I were at Clear Breeze Mountain, I meant to go and meet him. But by the time I arrived, I heard that he had already left, so fate denied us a meeting. So be it! Brother Kong Liang, if you want to save your elder brother, hurry there yourself and entreat them to come. We shall stay here and fight those wretches first.” Kong Liang entrusted his young bandits to Lu Zhishen and, taking only one attendant, disguised himself as a traveling merchant and journeyed day and night toward Liangshan Marsh.

p.src: Meanwhile, Lu Zhishen, Yang Zhi, and Wu Song returned to the stronghold and summoned Shi En and Cao Zheng, then brought another one or two hundred men down the mountain to reinforce them. When Li Zhong and Zhou Tong of Peach Blossom Mountain received the news, they mustered every man in their stronghold. Leaving only thirty or fifty young bandits to guard the stockade, they led all the rest down the mountain and gathered beneath the walls of Qingzhou to attack the city together. Of this, no more need be said for now.

p.src: Now Kong Liang, after leaving Qingzhou, traveled on until he reached the tavern of Li Li, the Life-Taking Judge, beside Liangshan Marsh, where he bought wine and asked the way. Seeing that the two men were strangers, Li Li invited them to sit and asked, “Where have you travelers come from?” Kong Liang replied, “From Qingzhou.” Li Li asked, “Whom do you seek at Liangshan Marsh?” Kong Liang answered, “I have an acquaintance on the mountain and have come especially to find him.” Li Li said, “The stronghold on the mountain is where the chieftains dwell. How could you possibly get there?” Kong Liang said, “It is Chieftain Song whom I seek.” Li Li said, “Since you have come to seek Chief Song, there is a customary allowance for you here.” He ordered the serving man to hurry and prepare the customary wine for his guests. Kong Liang said, “We have never met before. Why do you treat us so generously?” Li Li replied, “You do not understand, sir. Anyone who comes seeking a leader of our stronghold must be an old friend or comrade from the gallant fraternity. How could we dare neglect our duty to him? I shall report your arrival at once.” Kong Liang said, “I am none other than Kong Liang, a householder from the village below White Tiger Mountain.” Li Li said, “I have heard Brother Song Gongming speak of your honored name. How fortunate that you have come to the mountain today!” After the two had finished the customary wine, Li Li opened the window and loosed a signal arrow from the waterside pavilion. From deep among the reeds on the opposite shore, young bandits soon came rowing a boat across. When it reached the pavilion, Li Li invited Kong Liang aboard. Together they rowed to Golden Sands Beach, went ashore, and ascended to the pass. Seeing the imposing three passes and the spears, swords, blades, and halberds thick as a forest, Kong Liang thought, “I had heard that Liangshan Marsh was flourishing, but I never imagined they had built so mighty an enterprise!” A young bandit had already gone ahead to report his arrival, and Song Jiang hurried down to welcome him. At the sight of him, Kong Liang hurriedly bowed to the ground. Song Jiang asked, “What has brought you here, worthy brother?” When Kong Liang had finished his bow, he burst into loud sobs. Song Jiang said, “Whatever peril or insoluble trouble weighs upon you, worthy brother, tell me everything without reserve. I shall brave fire and water to deliver you from it and lend you all my strength. Please rise for now.” Kong Liang said, “After you left us, Master, our aged father passed away. My elder brother Kong Ming quarreled over some trifling matter with a wealthy household of our district and killed the entire family, old and young. The authorities pursued him relentlessly. So we rebelled and took to White Tiger Mountain, gathered five to seven hundred men, and began raiding houses and plundering travelers. But in Qingzhou city, our uncle Kong Bin was seized by Prefect Murong, fitted with a heavy cangue, and confined in prison. My brother and I therefore went to attack the city, hoping to rescue our uncle Kong Bin. But when we reached the walls, we ran straight into Huyan Zhuo, who wields a pair of steel whips. My brother fought him, but was captured and taken under guard to Qingzhou. He now lies in prison, and whether he lives or dies is uncertain. I too was pursued and attacked by him for some distance. The next day I happened to meet Wu Song. When I mentioned your great name, Master, he took me to meet his companions: one was Lu Zhishen, the Flowery Monk, and the other Yang Zhi, the Blue-Faced Beast. The two treated me as an old friend from our first meeting and at once discussed how to rescue my brother. They said, ‘We shall have Chiefs Lu and Yang join Li Zhong and Zhou Tong of Peach Blossom Mountain, muster the forces of all three mountains, and attack Qingzhou. You must hurry through the night to Liangshan Marsh, appeal to your master Song Gongming, and ask him to come save your uncle and elder brother.’ That is why I have come straight here today.” Song Jiang said, “This is easily dealt with. Set your mind at rest. First come and pay your respects to Chief Chao, so that we may discuss it together.” Song Jiang then led Kong Liang to pay his respects to Chao Gai, Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, and all the other chiefs. He explained in detail that Huyan Zhuo had fled to Qingzhou and sought refuge with Prefect Murong, that he had now captured Kong Ming, and that Kong Liang had therefore come to plead for their rescue.

p.src: Chao Gai said, “Since the heroes of those two places are still upholding righteousness and practicing benevolence, and since Third Brother is their dearest friend, how could we not go? Worthy brother, you have gone down the mountain many times in succession. Remain and guard the stronghold this time, while your foolish elder brother makes the journey in your stead.” Song Jiang said, “Elder brother, you are the master of the stronghold and must not move lightly. This is my own affair. Since he has come so far to seek my aid, if I do not go in person, I fear his brothers will feel uneasy. I ask only that several brothers accompany me on the journey.” Before he had finished speaking, everyone in the hall and below it cried out together, “We are ready to serve you like dogs and horses and follow you there!” Song Jiang was delighted. That day they laid a feast to entertain Kong Liang. During the feast, Song Jiang summoned Pei Xuan, the Iron-Faced Recorder, and ordered him to select the men who would descend the mountain and arrange them into five divisions: Hua Rong, Qin Ming, Yan Shun, and Wang the Short Tiger were assigned to the vanguard to open the road; Mu Hong, Yang Xiong, Xie Zhen, and Xie Bao were assigned to the second division; the central division consisted of the commander Song Jiang, Wu Yong, Lü Fang, and Guo Sheng; the fourth division consisted of Zhu Tong, Chai Jin, Li Jun, and Zhang Heng; and Sun Li, Yang Lin, Ou Peng, and Ling Zhen were assigned to the rear division to drive the army onward and guard its rear. Liangshan Marsh mustered five divisions in all: twenty chiefs and two thousand horsemen and foot soldiers. The remaining chiefs stayed with Chao Gai to guard the stronghold and its stockades. Song Jiang then took leave of Chao Gai and descended the mountain with Kong Liang. The troops of Liangshan set out in five divisions. Truly it was a sight of which one might say:

p.src: Newly departed from the watery stronghold, they were like dragons loosed within the four seas; Just emerged from Liangshan, they seemed like tigers and leopards racing before the wind. Five armies advanced together, with twenty heroes arrayed front and rear; Marching in a single host, three thousand soldiers stretched from van to rear. Embroidered banners billowed like clouds and mist; tempered blades glittered like spreading snow and frost. Phoenix bells rang as the warhorses galloped; Painted drums thundered as the warriors surged eagerly onward. Yellow dust rolled thickly across the earth, while a murky rain of soil filled the sky. Amid the great commander’s standard rode Wu the Scholar, rich in wisdom and resource; Beneath the green-oiled banner sat Song Gongming, who carried out Heaven’s justice. When they passed, even ghosts and gods bowed; when they returned, all the people sang their praises.

p.src: Now Song Jiang led twenty chiefs and three thousand troops from the Liangshan Marsh, divided into five armies advancing ahead. Nothing untoward occurred along the road, and as they passed through prefectures and counties, they did not take so much as a single autumn hair from the people. When they reached Qingzhou, Kong Liang went ahead to the army of Lu Zhishen and the others, informed the heroes of their arrival, and made preparations to receive them. When Song Jiang’s central army arrived, Wu Song brought Lu Zhishen, Yang Zhi, Li Zhong, Zhou Tong, Shi En, and Cao Zheng to meet him. Song Jiang invited Lu Zhishen to sit. Lu Zhishen said, “I have long heard of my elder brother’s great name, but chance never allowed me to pay my respects. Today I am delighted at last to make your acquaintance.” Song Jiang replied, “What worth is there in speaking of an untalented man like me? The righteous men of the rivers and lakes speak highly of the Master’s pure virtue. To behold your venerable countenance today is one of the greatest blessings of my life.” Yang Zhi also rose and bowed twice, saying, “When I passed through Liangshan Marsh in former days, the stronghold, esteeming righteousness, kindly urged me to remain. But I was foolish and misguided then and would not consent to stay. Today, fortunately, righteous heroes have magnificently strengthened the stronghold. This is the finest thing under Heaven.” Song Jiang replied, “Your Excellency’s martial fame is spread throughout the rivers and lakes. Song Jiang regrets only that our meeting came so late.” Lu Zhishen promptly ordered his attendants to set out wine and entertain them, and everyone was introduced in turn.

p.src: The next day, Song Jiang asked, “As for the affair at Qingzhou, how have victory and defeat stood lately?” Yang Zhi said, “Since Kong Liang left, we have fought three or five engagements, but neither side has won. At present, Qingzhou relies on Huyan Zhuo alone. If we can capture that man, taking this city will be as easy as pouring hot water over snow.” Wu the Scholar smiled and said, “This man cannot be overcome by force; he must be captured through stratagem.” Song Jiang asked, “What stratagem will capture him?” Wu the Scholar said, “We need only do thus and thus.” Song Jiang was overjoyed. “A splendid plan!” he exclaimed. That same day, the men and horses were assigned their parts. Early the next morning, the army set out and advanced to the foot of Qingzhou’s walls. Troops surrounded the city on every side, beating drums, waving banners, raising battle cries, and challenging the defenders to fight. Inside the city, Prefect Murong received the report and hurriedly summoned Huyan Zhuo to consult with him. “This time the bandits have again sent word to Song Jiang at Liangshan Marsh and brought him here. What are we to do now?” Huyan Zhuo said, “Set your mind at ease, Your Excellency. By coming here, the bandits have already forfeited the advantage of terrain. Those rogues can swagger only within their marsh. Now that they have rashly left their lair, I shall capture every one who comes. What opportunity can they have to display their tricks? Please ascend the wall, Your Excellency, and watch Huyan Zhuo do battle.” Huyan Zhuo hastily donned his armor, mounted his horse, ordered the city gate opened and the drawbridge lowered, and led out a thousand troops, whom he arrayed near the city. From Song Jiang’s battle line, a general rode forth. Holding a wolf-fanged mace, the man loudly cursed the prefect: “Corrupt official! Villain who preys upon the people! You slaughtered my entire family. Today is the perfect day to avenge them and wipe away my hatred!” Prefect Murong recognized Qin Ming and cursed him in reply: “You rogue! You were an official commissioned by the court, and the state never wronged you. Why have you dared to rebel? If you are captured, I shall have your body hacked into ten thousand pieces! Seize this rebel first!” Hearing this, Huyan Zhuo whirled his twin whips, spurred his horse, and charged straight at Qin Ming. Qin Ming likewise rode forth, brandishing his great wolf-fanged mace to meet Huyan Zhuo. The two generals met on horseback, evenly matched. A lyric to the tune “The Moon over the West River” bears witness:

p.src: The whips dance like two dragons’ tails; The mace sweeps crosswise, a row of wolves’ fangs. The watching hosts are dazzled, As the two generals wheel and clash on horseback. The mace-wielder is a leader among the ranks; The whip-wielder, scion of generals, merits praise. Heaven darkens, earth grows grim, and sand veils the sun; At such fierce combat, even ghosts and gods must quake.

p.src: The two fought for forty or fifty bouts without victory or defeat. Prefect Murong saw that they had fought a long while and feared some mishap might befall Huyan Zhuo, so he hurriedly sounded the gong and recalled the troops into the city. Qin Ming did not pursue him either, but withdrew to his own formation. Song Jiang ordered the chiefs, officers, and soldiers to withdraw fifteen li and make camp.

p.src: Now Huyan Zhuo returned inside the city, dismounted, and went to see Prefect Murong. He said, “I was just about to capture that Qin Ming. Why did Your Excellency recall the troops?” The prefect said, “I saw that you had fought for many bouts and feared only that you might be weary; therefore I recalled the army so you could rest awhile. That rogue Qin Ming was formerly a military commander here. He rebelled together with Hua Rong, and he too is an enemy not to be taken lightly.” Huyan Zhuo said, “Set your mind at ease, Your Excellency. I am determined to capture this traitorous rebel! When I fought him just now, his mace technique was already falling into disorder. Tomorrow, Your Excellency shall watch me behead that rebel on the spot!” The prefect said, “Since you are so valiant a hero, when you confront the enemy tomorrow, cut open a path and escort three men out: have one go to the Eastern Capital to seek aid; have the other two go to neighboring prefectures and provinces, assemble troops, and come assist us in suppressing and capturing the bandits.” Huyan Zhuo said, “Your Excellency’s wise judgment is perfectly clear.” That day, the prefect wrote letters requesting aid, selected three military officers, and dispatched each of them on his appointed mission.

p.src: Huyan Zhuo then returned to his quarters, removed his armor, and rested awhile. Before dawn, he heard an officer come to report: “On the earthen slope outside the north gate are three horsemen secretly observing the city. The man in the middle wears a red robe and rides a white horse. Of the two on either side, we recognize the one on the right as Hua Rong, the ‘Little Li Guang’; the man on the left is dressed as a Daoist.” Huyan Zhuo said, “The man in red is plainly Song Jiang, and the one dressed as a Daoist must be the strategist Wu Yong. Do not startle them yet. Muster a hundred cavalrymen at once and follow me to capture the three.”

p.src: Huyan Zhuo hurriedly armed himself and mounted, took up his twin whips, and led more than a hundred cavalrymen quietly out through the north gate. They lowered the drawbridge, and he led his troops in pursuit up the slope. Song Jiang, Wu Yong, and Hua Rong merely stared fixedly at the city, seemingly unaware of everything else. Huyan Zhuo spurred his horse up the slope. The three turned their mounts around and moved slowly away. Huyan Zhuo pursued with all his might until they reached several withered trees ahead. There Song Jiang, Wu Yong, and Hua Rong all reined in together. Just as Huyan Zhuo caught up to the dead trees, a sudden shout arose. He had stepped squarely onto a covered pit, and both horse and rider tumbled into it. Fifty or sixty men armed with hooked poles rushed out from both sides. First they hooked Huyan Zhuo out of the pit, bound him, and carried him away; afterward they led off his horse. As for the many cavalrymen who had followed, Hua Rong drew his bow and nocked an arrow, shooting down five or seven of those in front. The men behind wheeled their horses around and fled in a panicked mass.

p.src: Song Jiang returned to the stronghold and took his seat, whereupon the swordsmen on either side pushed Huyan Zhuo forward. At the sight of him, Song Jiang hurriedly rose and shouted, “Quickly, untie him!” He personally helped Huyan Zhuo into the command tent and seated him, then paid his respects. Huyan Zhuo said, “Why do you treat me so?” Song Jiang said, “How would a humble man like Song Jiang dare turn his back upon the imperial court? It was only because corrupt officials pressed me beyond endurance that I unwittingly committed a grave crime. Thus I have temporarily borrowed refuge here among the marshes, awaiting the day when the court pardons our offenses and offers us amnesty. I never intended to bring the general out against us and put you to such trouble. I have always admired your tiger-like might. Now that we have inadvertently offended you, I earnestly beg your forgiveness.” Huyan Zhuo said, “For one who has been captured, ten thousand deaths would scarcely atone. Why does a righteous gentleman treat me with such ceremony and offer such apologies?” Song Jiang said, “How could Song Jiang ever dare take the general’s life? High Heaven may bear witness to the sincerity of my heart.” He continued to entreat him most earnestly. Huyan Zhuo said, “Is it your honored wish, elder brother, that I go to the Eastern Capital to petition for an offer of amnesty and a pardon for the stronghold?” Song Jiang said, “How could you possibly go, General? That scoundrel Grand Marshal Gao is a narrow-hearted man who forgets great favors but remembers the smallest offense. You have lost so many troops, horses, funds, and provisions—how could he fail to hold you accountable? Han Tao, Peng Qi, and Ling Zhen have already joined our humble mountain band. If you would not disdain the lowliness of our stronghold, I would gladly yield my place to you. When the court has use for us and we have accepted amnesty, it will not be too late then to devote ourselves loyally to the service of the realm.”

p.src: The men atop the wall recognized Huyan Zhuo’s voice and hurried to report to Prefect Murong. At the time, the prefect was brooding over the loss of Huyan Zhuo. When told that Huyan Zhuo had escaped and returned, he was delighted, mounted at once, and hastened to the city wall. He saw Huyan Zhuo with more than ten riders behind him. Their faces were indistinct, and he recognized only Huyan Zhuo’s voice. The prefect asked, “General, how did you manage to escape and return?” Huyan Zhuo said, “Those scoundrels caught me in a pitfall and carried me to their stronghold. But some officers who formerly served under me secretly stole this horse for me to ride and came away with me.” As soon as the prefect heard Huyan Zhuo’s account, he ordered the soldiers to open the city gate and lower the drawbridge. The ten chieftains followed him through the gate. As they came face-to-face with the prefect, Qin Ming struck Prefect Murong with one blow of his club and knocked him from his horse. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao immediately started fires. Ou Peng and Wang the Short Tiger rushed up onto the wall and scattered the soldiers by force. When Song Jiang’s main force saw the flames rise from the wall, they surged into the city together. Song Jiang urgently issued orders that no harm be done to the common people and that the money and grain in the treasuries and granaries be secured; then they rescued Kong Ming from the great prison, together with his uncle Kong Bin and his entire household, and ordered the fires extinguished. Every member of Prefect Murong’s household, young and old, was beheaded. His property was confiscated and distributed among the troops. At daybreak, they counted the city households whose homes had burned and distributed grain and rice to relieve them. They loaded the gold and silks from the prefectural treasury and the rice and grain from the granaries onto five or six hundred carts, and also obtained more than two hundred fine horses. Then they held a celebratory feast in Qingzhou Prefecture and invited the chieftains of the three mountains to return with them to the great stronghold. Li Zhong and Zhou Tong sent men back to Peach Blossom Mountain to bring down all their troops, funds, and provisions, then set fire to and destroyed the stockade. Lu Zhishen likewise sent Shi En and Cao Zheng back to Twin Dragons Mountain, where they joined Zhang Qing and Sun Erniang in gathering the troops, funds, and provisions, and burned down the Precious Pearl Monastery stockade as well. Within a few days, the forces of all three mountains had completed their preparations. Song Jiang led the main force on its triumphant return to the mountain. He sent the four generals Hua Rong, Qin Ming, Huyan Zhuo, and Zhu Tong ahead to clear the road, and they did not disturb the prefectures and counties they passed through by so much as a penny. The country folk supported the old and led the young out to meet them, burning incense and bowing in rows. After several days, they reached the shore of Liangshan Marsh. The many naval chieftains came out in boats to welcome them. Chao Gai led the cavalry and infantry chieftains of the stronghold to welcome them at Golden Sands Beach. They proceeded directly to the great stronghold, where they took their places in the Hall of Righteous Assembly. A grand banquet was laid to celebrate the twelve chieftains newly arrived at the stronghold: Huyan Zhuo, Lu Zhishen, Yang Zhi, Wu Song, Shi En, Cao Zheng, Zhang Qing, Sun Erniang, Li Zhong, Zhou Tong, Kong Ming, and Kong Liang. During the feast, Lin Chong spoke of his gratitude to Lu Zhishen for once saving him. Lu Zhishen asked, “Since I parted from the Instructor at Cangzhou, have you received any news of your wife?” Lin Chong replied, “After I killed Wang Lun in the clash, I sent men home to bring my family here. I then learned that my poor wife, driven beyond endurance by Grand Marshal Gao’s wicked son, had hanged herself soon afterward. Her father, too, fell ill from grief and anxiety and died.” Yang Zhi brought up the time when he had come to the mountain and met them under Wang Lun. Everyone said, “All this was predestined—it was no accident!” Chao Gai recounted the robbery of the birthday gifts at Yellow Mud Ridge, and everyone burst into laughter. The next day they took turns hosting banquets, but of this there is no need to speak further.

p.src: Now when Song Jiang saw that so many more men and horses had joined the stronghold, how could he not rejoice? He appointed Tang Long chief superintendent of the smithies, placing him in charge of forging every kind of weapon, together with iron-plated linked armor and the like; Hou Jian was made chief superintendent of banners and uniforms, with orders to make additional flags of the Three Powers, Nine Luminaries, Four Dippers, Five Directions, and Twenty-eight Mansions, as well as Flying Dragon, Flying Tiger, Flying Bear, and Flying Leopard standards, yellow battle-axes, white yak-tail streamers, scarlet tassels, and black canopies. Watchtowers were built on all four sides of the mountain. The two inns on the western and southern approaches were rebuilt to receive worthy men traveling up the mountain, while also gathering intelligence and swiftly reporting military developments. The inn on the western road was now entrusted to the married couple Zhang Qing and Sun Erniang, who had formerly kept an inn themselves; the inn on the southern road remained in the care of the married couple Sun Xin and Mistress Gu; the inn on the eastern road remained with Zhu Gui and Yue He; and the inn on the northern road remained with Li Li and Shi Qian. Stockades were added at the three passes, and chieftains were assigned in turn to guard them. Once the assignments had been settled, everyone obeyed his orders; no more need be said of it.

p.src: Then one day Lu Zhishen, the Flowery Monk, came to Song Gongming and said, “I have an acquaintance whom Brother Li Zhong also knows. His name is Shi Jin, the Nine-Dragoned. He is now on Mount Shaohua in Huayin County, Huazhou, where he has gathered in brotherhood with Zhu Wu, the Resourceful Strategist, Chen Da, the Gorge-Leaping Tiger, and Yang Chun, the White-Flowered Serpent. I often think of him. Long ago, at the Earthenware Jar Temple, he came to my aid, and I have never forgotten it. I wish to go there and visit him, then bring all four of them back to join us. What do you think?” Song Jiang said, “I too have heard of Shi Jin’s great name. It would be best indeed if you, Master, would go and invite him here. Even so, you must not go alone. I would trouble Brother Wu Song to accompany you. He is a pilgrim, a religious man like yourself, and so is the perfect traveling companion.” Wu Song answered, “I shall go with Master.” That same day they packed their bags and baggage. Lu Zhishen dressed simply as a mendicant monk, while Wu Song disguised himself as the monk’s attendant pilgrim. The two took leave of the assembled chieftains and descended the mountain. After crossing Golden Sands Strand, they traveled by day and lodged by night, and after several days reached the borders of Huayin County in Huazhou, heading straight for Mount Shaohua.

p.src: Meanwhile, when Lu Zhishen and Wu Song reached the foot of Mount Shaohua, some bandit sentries lying in ambush came out to bar their way and demanded, “Where have you two men of religion come from?” Wu Song replied, “Is Master Shi on this mountain?” The bandit said, “If you have come seeking Chief Shi, wait here a moment. I shall go up the mountain and inform our chiefs, who will soon come down to welcome you.” Wu Song said, “Just tell them that Lu Zhishen has come to visit him.” The bandit had not been gone long when Zhu Wu, the Resourceful Strategist, Chen Da, the Gorge-Leaping Tiger, and Yang Chun, the White-Flowered Serpent, came down the mountain to welcome Lu Zhishen and Wu Song—but Shi Jin was nowhere to be seen. Lu Zhishen immediately asked, “Where is Master Shi? Why do I not see him?” Zhu Wu stepped forward and respectfully asked, “Master, are you not Major Lu of Yan’an Prefecture?” Lu Zhishen said, “That is who I am. This pilgrim is Wu Song, the constable who slew the tiger on Jingyang Ridge.” The three hurriedly made obeisance, saying, “We have long heard of your great names! We heard that you two had established a stronghold on Mount Twin Dragons. What brings you here today?” Lu Zhishen said, “We are no longer on Mount Twin Dragons. We have gone to join Song Gongming’s great stronghold at Liangshan Marsh. We have come especially to seek Master Shi.” Zhu Wu said, “Since you have both come this far, please first enter our stronghold, and allow me to explain everything in detail.” Lu Zhishen said, “If you have something to say, say it now! Who the devil has patience to wait?” Wu Song said, “Master is a hasty man. If there is something to tell us, what harm is there in saying it now?”

p.src: Zhu Wu said, “The three of us have kept this mountain stronghold, and since Master Shi came up here, it has prospered greatly. Recently, while Master Shi was down from the mountain, he happened upon a painter from Daming Prefecture in the Northern Capital, whose surname was Wang and personal name was Yi. He had vowed to paint the spirit wall in the temple of the Great Sage of the Golden Heaven on Mount Hua, the Western Sacred Peak, and had gone there to fulfill his vow. He had brought along his daughter, Yujiaozhi. But the prefect of Huazhou, He—who was a protégé of Grand Tutor Cai and was such a greedy, corrupt official that he cruelly oppressed the people—came one day to burn incense at the temple. There he happened to see that Yujiaozhi was beautiful, and repeatedly sent men to propose taking her as his concubine. When Wang Yi refused, the prefect seized his daughter by force and made her his concubine, then sentenced Wang Yi to penal exile in a distant and pestilential military district. As he was escorted past this place, he happened to meet Master Shi and told him what had happened. Master Shi rescued Wang Yi and brought him up the mountain, killed the two constables escorting him, then went straight to the prefectural seat intending to assassinate Prefect He. But he was discovered and captured instead, and is now confined in prison. They also plan to muster troops and sweep away our stronghold. We are here at our wits’ end!” When Lu Zhishen heard this, he cried, “How dare that pack of scoundrels behave so outrageously! So they think themselves that formidable! I’ll go finish the bastard off for you!” Zhu Wu said, “Please, both of you, come up to the stronghold first so that we may discuss the matter.” The five chieftains went together to the stronghold on Mount Shaohua and sat down. They summoned Wang Yi to meet Lu Zhishen and Wu Song, and he told them how Prefect He greedily and cruelly oppressed the people and forcibly seized respectable women. As he was escorted past this place, he happened to meet Master Shi and told him what had happened.

p.src: Now Lu Zhishen hurried into the city of Huazhou and asked a passerby where the prefectural offices were. The man pointed and said, “Just cross the prefectural bridge and head east.” Lu Zhishen had just reached the pontoon bridge when everyone said, “Master, step aside for a moment—the prefect is coming.” Lu Zhishen said, “He is the very man I have come to find. What luck that he should fall straight into my hands! The scoundrel must surely be fated to die!” Prefect He’s advance guards came filing past in pairs, and then the prefect’s sedan appeared—a covered, heated chair. On either side of its windows clustered ten attendants, each armed with a barbed staff or iron chain, guarding the chair from both flanks. Seeing this, Lu Zhishen thought, “This is no good. If I strike at that bastard and miss him, I shall only make myself a laughingstock.” From the window of his sedan, Prefect He noticed Lu Zhishen wavering over whether to approach. After crossing the Wei Bridge and alighting at his residence, he summoned two attendants and ordered them, “Go invite that big, burly monk on the bridge to come to my residence for a vegetarian meal.” The attendants received their orders, went to the bridge, and said to Lu Zhishen, “His Excellency the prefect invites you to a vegetarian feast.” Lu Zhishen thought, “This scoundrel is surely destined to die by my hand. Just now I meant to strike him, but feared I might miss, and so I let him pass. I was looking for him, and now he has sent to invite me.” Lu Zhishen thereupon followed the attendants straight to the prefect’s residence. The prefect had already given his instructions. As soon as Lu Zhishen reached the front of the hall, he was told to surrender his monk’s staff and remove his戒刀, then invited into the rear hall for the meal. At first Lu Zhishen refused, but the others said, “For a man of religion, you have precious little sense. How could you be permitted to carry a blade and staff into the inner chambers of the prefectural residence?” Lu Zhishen thought, “With these two fists alone, I can still smash that scoundrel’s skull!” He left his monk’s staff and戒刀 beneath the gallery and followed the attendants inside. Prefect He was seated in the rear hall. With a wave of his hand, he shouted, “Seize this bald-headed brigand!” Thirty or forty constables burst from behind the hangings on either side and, hauling and wrenching him to the ground, seized Lu Zhishen. Even were you Prince Nezha himself, how could you escape this all-encompassing net of earth and heaven? Even a fire-headed guardian deity could scarcely escape this dragon’s pool and tiger’s den. Indeed: the moth that flies into the flame must lose its body; the angry turtle that swallows the hook must forfeit its life. As for what became of Lu Zhishen’s life after Prefect He had him arrested, listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
